heuristics.description: This is the initial knowledge base file. Every time a new compiler trick or C structure is discovered to match PS1/PsyQ assembly perfectly, an entry should be added here.

The .c files are compiled using tools/gcc-2.6.0-psx/cc1 (or 2.7.2). The assembler output is passed through tools/maspsx/maspsx.py to translate PsyQ syntax to GNU MIPS, then assembled by mips-linux-gnu-as. It is crucial to use mips-linux-gnu tools.

The project uses `splat` to carve `disc/SLUS_006.64` based on `config/slus_006.64.yaml` into `src/` (C) and `asm/` (assembly). `objdiff` verifies matches headlessly and outputs to `build/progress.json`.

heuristics.concept: PS1 Disc Format and Custom Overlays
heuristics.description: Standard disc images like `.mdf` often use 2448-byte sectors (with 96-byte padding). These must be stripped to 2352-byte standard `.bin` format using `tools/scripts/strip_mdf.py`. Xenogears stores its overlays (FIELD.BIN, MOVIE.BIN) inside custom LZSS compressed CD sectors, which cannot be seen via standard ISO 9660. The repository provides `tools/scripts/extract_overlays.py` to carve these directly from `Xenogears.bin`.

Always consult `tools/` before writing external scripts. Available utilities: `maspsx/` (translates PsyQ assembly to GNU MIPS), `objdiff/` (binary diffing), `gcc-*/` (various PS1 compilers), `tools/scripts/ghidra_import_splat_symbols.py` (for Ghidra ROM labeling), `tools/scripts/get_yaml_target.py` (splat config parser), `tools/scripts/ci_extract_assets.sh` (1-click LZSS disk extraction wrapper), and `tools/scripts/generate_call_graph.py` (assembly analysis tool for identifying easy/leaf functions).

If `maspsx.py` is mysteriously missing before or during `make build`, it means the repository submodules were not initialized properly. Run `git submodule update --init --recursive`. If `make check` fails with 'no file was verified', check the line endings of `config/checksum.sha`. It must be converted to Unix style via `dos2unix` for standard Linux `sha256sum` to parse it correctly.

patterns.description: Example: If the compiler uses v0 instead of s0, try assigning the struct pointer to a volatile local variable before the loop.

If MIPS assembly contains isolated `sb` (store byte) or `lb` (load byte) instructions against a defined struct pointer (e.g., `sb $a1, 0xB0($a0)`), but the struct definition at that offset hasn't been fully mapped to a bitfield yet, you can reliably generate perfectly matching code by casting the pointer to a byte array and accessing the index directly: `((u8*)ptr)[0xB0] = val;`

Never use `make report` in the middle of a continuous AI evaluation loop. Executing `make report` or `make expected` artificially rebuilds empty `.o` files without assembly to provide a baseline for `objdiff`. This overwrites standard compiler objects. Doing `make build` immediately after will result in massive undefined linker errors because GCC thinks the files are up-to-date and avoids compiling them. You must run `make clean-build` after any report generation to reset the development cache. For rapid iteration on a single file, exclusively use `make build`.

patterns.concept: Forced Register Allocation via GCC 'asm' Extensions
patterns.description: If your C code logic matches the assembly perfectly, but GCC chooses different temporary arithmetic registers (e.g., you need `$a2` and `$v0`, but GCC uses `$a0` and `$v0`), you can force the compiler's hand using GCC Local Register Variables: `register int a2 asm("a2") = expression;`. This is an extremely powerful technique to achieve byte-for-byte matching on mathematically simple functions that otherwise fail the `objdiff` hash due to arbitrary register assignment.

When renaming an unintuitive generated label (like func_800295D8 or D_8004FE18) into a meaningful human-readable C name, you MUST execute a global search-and-replace across the entire repository. This includes: src/ (.c), include/ (.h), asm/ (.s), config/ (.txt symbol maps), and yaml/ (Splat definitions). Failure to update the YAML or config strings will cause catastrophic 'undefined reference' linker errors during make check, because the compiled objects will attempt to link against the previous arbitrary name.

patterns.concept: GCC 2.7.2 Infinite Spin Loop Optimization Mismatches
patterns.description: When decompiling PsyQ hardware spin routines (like `while(flag & 0x10) {}`), PsyQ literally compiles `lui` and `lhu` load instructions directly inside the loop branch. Modern GCC perfectly translates this with the `volatile` keyword. However, old MIPS GCC 2.7.2 is notoriously stubborn about loop-invariant code motion (hoisting). It will frequently pull the pointer setup `lui` instruction outside the loop branch and only re-execute `lhu`, completely breaking byte-for-byte matching. Standard tricks like local `extern volatile short` or inline empty `asm("")` barriers often fail to perfectly replicate the original PsyQ `lui/lhu` tight coupling. If a spin loop fails matching due to hoisted registers, it is acceptable (and often necessary) to leave it as `INCLUDE_ASM` rather than writing convoluted unreadable C.

patterns.concept: Enforcing Module Header Encapsulation for Externs
patterns.description: Never place floating `extern void Foo();` or `extern u32 Bar[];` declarations directly inside a `.c` file unless it genuinely acts strictly as a static/private workaround (which is extremely rare). Doing so fundamentally breaks architectural encapsulation and produces unmaintainable C code. If an undefined external reference is mapped during decompilation, it MUST be declared within its corresponding public header file (e.g., `include/system/sound.h`). The source file then uses `#include "system/sound.h"` to resolve the symbols. This enforces strict architectural boundaries across the Xenogears decompilation effort.

GCC 2.6.0 will happily lift memory assignments (e.g. `newEntry->pNext = NULL;`) into the delay slots of subsequent function calls (e.g. `EnableEvent()`). If a decompiled function logically matches but order is slightly 'off' resulting in mismatched delay slots, try placing the assignments directly *before* the function call to see if the compiler hoists them natively into the delay slot.

A standard modern `while(curr->next)` loop evaluates differently in PsyQ. To match original PS1 linked list traversals exactly, you frequently must use a pre-condition `if (head != NULL)` followed by a `do { ... } while (curr != NULL);` loop. This forces GCC to emit the exact 6-instruction loop footprint seen in many of Xenogears' list iterations.

patterns.concept: Struct Black Box Explosion via Initializers
patterns.description: When faced with a giant `unknown_data[0xNN]` array inside a struct, search for its initialization function in the assembly logic. Because the object initializer must manually reset the inner bytes to zero/default values, decompiling the initializer function quickly uncovers the explicit `u8`, `u16`, and `u32` variables hidden inside the array.

patterns.concept: Flat Goto Block Manipulation for Branch Polarity
patterns.description: By default, GCC compiles structured `if(cond) { block } else { block }` by emitting an inverted check `beqz` that branches over the true block to the false block. However, if the original assembly uses explicit true-branches (`bnez`, `beq`) that jump to distant memory locations and organically fall-through, you cannot match this with nested `if/else` statements. You must write flat C code that completely separates the conditional checks from the execution blocks using explicit `goto` commands mapping 1-to-1 with the original assembly structure.

patterns.concept: Mandatory Doxygen and Assembly Inline Documentation
patterns.description: Any successfully decompiled/matched C function MUST be immediately documented with a Doxygen block (`/** ... */`) explaining its purpose, parameters, and return type. Furthermore, you must inline comment any odd C logic mapping back to specific assembly quirks (e.g. `// required to match lui/lhu hoisting` or `// handwritten inline assembly for Coprocessor 2 ctc2 instructions`). Never skip the final documentation step.

patterns.concept: GCC Branch Delay Slot Assignment Placement
patterns.description: If a memory assignment (e.g. `start = pDst`) needs to be pushed into the branch delay slot of an immediately following condition (like `if (size <= 0)`), placing the assignment operation *after required early returns* but directly before the condition block allows GCC to effectively tuck the operation into the MIPS delay slot natively instead of executing it before evaluating the condition. This trick is essential for 1-to-1 matching in memory-tight standard library functions like `memcpy`.

patterns.concept: GCC 2.7.2 Return Crossjumping and Delay Slot Masking
patterns.description: When multiple early exits or paths return `NULL` (or the same variable) from a function, GCC 2.7.2 will aggressively 'crossjump' (merge) the return paths into a singular block at the bottom of the function. This explicitly destroys handwritten or unoptimized PsyQ assembly logic which expects to natively populate `move v0, zero` inside the branch delay slots. To bypass return crossjumping and force GCC to embed the variable assignment into the specific delay slot of a True Branch (bgtz, beqz, etc.), you must abandon multiple `return` statements and `if/else` logic. Instead, initialize a single tracking variable (e.g. `start = NULL`), and use purely flat `goto` structures explicitly pointing to a single `end:` label which executes the final `return start;`. This tricks the compiler into emitting the branch exactly where defined and tucking the return variable into its delay slot locally.

patterns.concept: PS1 BIOS Tail-Call Wrappers Are Permanently INCLUDE_ASM
patterns.description: Many PsyQ SDK functions (libapi, libapi_2, libapi_3, libcard) are 3-instruction BIOS dispatch trampolines: `addiu $t2, $zero, 0xB0; jr $t2; addiu $t1, $zero, <func_num>`. These jump to the PS1 kernel's A0/B0/C0 dispatch tables and never return to the wrapper — the BIOS function returns directly to the original caller. Because GCC always emits a `jr $ra; nop` epilogue on any C function (even with `__asm__ volatile`), these 3-instruction (12-byte) functions cannot be expressed in C — GCC would produce 5 instructions (20 bytes). There is no `__attribute__((naked))` in GCC 2.7.2 for MIPS. Similarly, `setjmp`/`longjmp` directly manipulate callee-saved registers and `$ra`, making them fundamentally inexpressible in C. These were hand-written assembly in the original PsyQ SDK and must remain as `INCLUDE_ASM` permanently. Do NOT waste time attempting to decompile them. Known affected functions: StartPAD2, InitPAD2, StopPAD2, SysEnqIntRP, SysDeqIntRP, HookEntryInt, ResetEntryInt, ReturnFromException, ChangeClearRCnt, StartCARD2, InitCARD2, StopCARD2, _card_info, func_80040ABC, func_8004BED8, setjmp, longjmp.

patterns.concept: Flat Goto Pattern Reuse Across libc Functions
patterns.description: The flat goto + delay slot masking pattern (pattern_example_013) is not unique to a single function — it is a systematic compiler idiom used across the entire PsyQ libc. Functions `bzero`, `memset`, and `memchr` all use the identical structure: (1) NULL-check early return, (2) `if (size > 0) { start = pDst; goto loop; }`, (3) `start = NULL; goto end;`, (4) do-while loop, (5) single `return start;` at the `end:` label. When encountering a new libc-style function with multiple return paths and delay-slot-seated v0 assignments, try this template first — it matched on the first attempt for `memset` because the pattern was already proven on `bzero`.

patterns.concept: PsyQ GPU Vtable Dispatch Pattern (GpuPackage struct)
patterns.description: Many PsyQ libgpu functions dispatch through `g_GpuPkg`, a `GpuPackage*` struct pointer (renamed from D_800568C8). The struct is defined in include/psyq/libgpu.h with a mix of function pointers (K&R style `()` for unspecified args) and u_long data members. Function pointers use K&R `()` so callers don't need casts — GCC 2.7.2 treats `()` as accepting any arguments. Key struct members: transfer (0x08) = DMA transfer function, clearParam (0x0C), command (0x10) = GP1 command sender, sendData (0x14) = primitive data sender, otagParam (0x18), storeParam (0x1C), loadParam (0x20), clearOTagR (0x2C), reset (0x34), drawSync (0x3C). Example: `g_GpuPkg->drawSync(mode)` replaces `((int (*)(int))D_800568C8[0xF])(mode)` with identical codegen. The struct approach produces byte-perfect matches because sizeof(function_ptr) == sizeof(u_long) == 4 on MIPS32, so struct layout is identical to the original u_long array.

patterns.concept: Temp Variable Ordering Controls Register Allocation and Evaluation Order in OR Chains
patterns.description: When GCC 2.7.2 evaluates a multi-operand OR expression like `(b << 16) | ((g << 8) | 0x80000000) | r`, it freely reassociates the OR chain (since OR is commutative+associative), ignoring explicit parentheses. This can cause: (1) wrong register allocation (s0/s1 swapped for variables), and (2) wrong evaluation order (0x80000000 ORed with the wrong operand). The fix is to split the expression into separate assignment statements with explicit temp variables: `bv = b << 16; color = (g << 8) | 0x80000000; return f(bv | color | r);`. This forces GCC to: (a) allocate the first-assigned variable to s0 and the second to s1, and (b) evaluate the statements in declaration order, preventing reassociation across statement boundaries. Discovered during ClearImage2 decompilation where 5 expression variants failed before the temp-variable approach matched byte-for-byte. Note: single temp variables can fix grouping but may produce wrong evaluation order (g-part before b-part); TWO temps are needed when both register allocation AND evaluation order matter.

patterns.concept: Inverted If-Body Pattern Produces bnez Without Goto
patterns.description: When the target assembly uses `bnez` (forward branch over an error path to the main body), the natural C pattern `if (cond == 0) return -1;` produces `beqz` (wrong polarity). Previous approaches required flat goto state-machines to force `bnez`. However, wrapping the body in `if (cond) { body; return result; } return -1;` naturally produces `bnez` because GCC lays out the blocks as: (1) test cond, (2) error path inline (`j exit; li -1`), (3) body after. The `bnez` jumps OVER the error path to the body. This is much cleaner than goto and avoids convergence-induced register allocation conflicts. Combine with `register int dest asm("$2")` to pin the return value register and route all intermediate values (width check, height check, packed result, rect data) through the same pinned variable, eliminating extra `move` instructions at merge points. Discovered during MoveImage decompilation (attempt 24 of 24): the `if (dest) { body; return dest; }` pattern produced byte-perfect branch structure (beqz for width, bnez for height, correct delay slots) with zero goto statements. Key insight: `if (x == 0) return err;` gives beqz (early exit), while `if (x) { work; return ok; } return err;` gives bnez (jump over error to body) — same logic, different block layout.
